title: The missing reverse bound is the witness-spread realizer of the super-code list
evidence: C014 claims the missing reverse bound I(delta) >= poly*|list(RS[k+1],delta)| is 'pinned' by the two in-tree MCAWitnessSpread lemmas (unique_bad_gamma_common_witness + common_witness_badGamma_set_card_le_one), realizable as a 'section' c -> (gamma_c=-coeff_k(c), S_c) of the RS[k+1] super-code list, provable by composing epsMCA_ge_card_div_of_mcaEvent_set with the contrapositive of the common-witness lemma. REFUTED on two independent grounds. (1) LOGICAL NON-SEQUITUR: common_witness_badGamma_set_card_le_one is a one-directional COLLAPSE bound (G of bad scalars sharing ONE no-joint-pair witness S => |G|<=1). Its contrapositive gives a NECESSARY spread condition for a large bad set; the reverse bound needs the CONVERSE (a spread of witness sets/list elements => many BAD scalars), which the lemma does not provide. And epsMCA_ge_card_div_of_mcaEvent_set CONSUMES a set of gamma already known bad -- it cannot manufacture bad gamma from list elements. The proposed composition has no theorem that turns a list element into a bad scalar, so it does not constitute a proof. (2) EXACT PROBE at a genuinely PROPER subgroup mu_8 subset F_233 (n^2=64 < q=233, q=1 mod 8, prize-shaped n<<sqrt(q)), monomial line u1=X^k, k=1, exhaustive over RS[k+1]=q^2 codewords and exact bad-scalar computation per received word u0 (scripts/probes/_407_conn/probe_C014_reverse_witness_spread.py, exact integer arithmetic, exit 0). At the high-radius prize regime t=1 (delta=0.875): forward bound I<=|list| holds (sanity, maxI=28<=maxList=1838); but the REVERSE collapses: worst-case I/|list| = 0.013 (one stack has I=23 bad scalars vs |list|=1837 RS[k+1] codewords). The C014 'section' fails BOTH requirements: (a) NOT injective -- distinct list codewords share leading coefficients (sec_noninj=True); (b) image NOT in the bad set -- only 1591 of 13980 listed gamma (~11%) are actually bad; the other ~89% have a joint codeword pair on their agreement set so mcaEvent never fires. The single-code list at radius delta is ~65x the bad count and is NOT a lower-bound realizer. (3) The CORRECT reverse object is already in-tree: mcaBad_card_le_interleavedList (InterleavedListMCACollapse.lean) and DISPROOF_LOG O85/O89 prove the governing quantity is the INTERLEAVED list Lambda_2 at the DOUBLED radius 2delta, not the single-code RS[k+1] list at radius delta -- the probe's maxLambda2=0 at t=1 matches I being tiny while |list| is huge.
honest_note: The FORWARD bridge (badScalars_monomial_card_le_listSize: I<=|list(RS[k+1])|) is genuine, proven, and axiom-clean -- that half is correct. The two MCAWitnessSpread lemmas are also correct and useful, but only as the NECESSARY-condition (collapse/upper-bound) half: 'a large bad set forces distinct witness sets.' C014's error is reading them as the SUFFICIENT half ('distinct witness sets / a large list => a large bad set'), which is the reverse implication and is false. Not a closure failure of the prize -- this connection does not touch BGK/Paley sqrt-cancellation at all; it is a structural mis-identification of which combinatorial object bounds I(delta) below. The genuine reverse object (interleaved Lambda_2 at doubled radius, with explicit loss 2(n-t)) was already isolated and proven in-tree before this connection, so there is no new reduction. The numeric refutation (section non-injective, ~89% of listed gamma not bad, worst I/list=0.013 at a proper subgroup) should be appended to DISPROOF_LOG.md alongside O85/O89.
